claim: The General Assembly meets on the Wednesday after the first Monday of January in odd-numbered years
citation: Conn. Const. art. III, § 2 (as amended by amend. art. III)
quote: on the Wednesday following the first Monday of January in the odd-numbered years

claim: An odd-year session adjourns by the first Wednesday after the first Monday in June
quote: shall adjourn each regular session in the odd-numbered years not later than the first Wednesday after the first Monday in June

claim: After adjournment the governor has fifteen days from presentment to veto
quote: within fifteen calendar days after the same has been presented to him

claim: During the session the governor has five days
quote: within five calendar days, Sundays and legal holidays excepted

claim: Bills can be presented to the governor after adjournment
quote: Bills may be presented to the governor after the adjournment of the general assembly

claim: A veto session is called on the second Monday after the governor's last day to return vetoes
quote: the secretary of the state shall reconvene the general assembly on the second Monday after the last day on which the governor is authorized to transmit

claim: Public acts take effect on 1 October after the session unless the act says otherwise
quote: shall take effect on the first day of October following the session of the General Assembly at which they are passed

claim: Since 2022 every municipality holds its regular election biennially in November of odd-numbered years
quote: there shall be held in each municipality, biennially, a municipal election on the Tuesday after the first Monday of November of the odd-numbered years

claim: A municipality may instead vote on the first Monday of May of odd years by a three-fourths vote of its legislative body
quote: may be held on the first Monday of May of the odd-numbered years if the legislative body of such municipality so determines by a three-fourths vote

claim: A May town can move back to November by majority vote
quote: may subsequently determine by a majority vote to hold such municipal election on the Tuesday after the first Monday of November of the odd-numbered years

claim: Probate judges are elected by district every four years, counting from 1966
quote: Judges of probate shall be elected by the electors residing in their respective districts on the Tuesday after the first Monday of November, 1966, and quadrennially thereafter

claim: Primaries for state offices are on the second Tuesday in August
quote: shall be held on the second Tuesday in August in the year in which such state election is held

claim: Municipal primaries are held 56 days before the election
quote: shall be held on the fifty-sixth day preceding the day of the election

claim: Only enrolled party members vote in a party primary, plus unaffiliated voters if the party's rules allow
quote: he is on the last-completed enrollment list of such party in the municipality or voting district

claim: Unaffiliated voters may vote only if authorized by the party's state rules
quote: if authorized by the state rules of such party filed pursuant to section

claim: Party-endorsed municipal candidates are chosen by caucus, convention or town committee
quote: shall be selected, in accordance with the rules of such party, by: (1) The enrolled members of such party in such municipality in caucus

claim: A primary is held only if someone other than the endorsed candidate files to challenge
quote: is filed by or on behalf of any person other than a party-endorsed candidate within the applicable time specified in section

claim: Ballots list candidates by party row, with petitioning candidates after the parties
quote: Petitioning candidates with no party designation whose names are contained in petitions approved pursuant to section

claim: Ballot rows are ordered by the parties' votes for governor
quote: The party whose candidate for Governor polled the highest number of votes in the last-preceding election

claim: Winners are decided by plurality
quote: when at any such election the plurality of an elected candidate for an office over the vote for a defeated candidate receiving the next highest number of votes

claim: Minority representation caps how many members of a board may be from one party
quote: who may be members of the same political party, shall be as specified in the following table

claim: Above nine members the cap is two-thirds
quote: More than 9

claim: The cap does not apply to bodies elected by district or to a town meeting
quote: whose members are elected wholly or partially on the basis of a geographical division of the state or political subdivision

claim: Unless a charter says otherwise, a town elects selectmen, town clerk, treasurer, tax collector, constables, registrars and board of education
quote: Unless otherwise provided by special act or charter, (1) members of boards of assessment appeals, (2) selectmen, (3) town clerks, (4) town treasurers, (5) collectors of taxes, (6) constables, (7) registrars of voters

claim: A town may appoint its clerk, treasurer or tax collector by ordinance instead
quote: a town clerk, town treasurer or collector of taxes in lieu of the election of such officers

claim: Unless otherwise provided, a town elects a first selectman and two other selectmen (up to six in towns of 10,000+)
quote: elect a first selectman, who shall be town agent unless otherwise provided by law, and two other selectmen

claim: Votes for a losing first selectman candidate count toward a seat on the board
quote: for an unsuccessful candidate for first selectman shall be counted as votes for him as a member of such board

claim: Voters may not vote for more selectmen than one party can elect
quote: an elector shall not vote for more candidates for the office of selectman than a political party can elect pursuant to section

claim: Municipal terms default to two years
quote: when not otherwise prescribed by law, shall be for two years

claim: Chief executives, selectmen and legislative bodies serve two- or four-year terms set by charter or ordinance
quote: as prescribed by charter or ordinance shall be two years or four years

claim: A board of education has 3, 6, 9 or 12 members unless a special act provides otherwise
quote: The board of education in each town shall consist of three, six, nine or twelve residents of such town

claim: Limited voting: voters choose no more than half (or a bare majority) of the school board seats up
quote: no elector shall vote for more than half that number

claim: Connecticut has eight counties, each a list of towns
quote: There shall be in the state eight counties

claim: County government ended in 1960; county powers passed to the state
quote: all powers and authority of said counties shall be vested in the state

claim: Home rule: the General Assembly delegates power to towns, cities and boroughs by general law and sets maximum terms
quote: The general assembly shall from time to time by general law determine the maximum terms of office of the various town, city and borough elective offices

claim: No special acts for a single town, city or borough on its organization or terms of office
quote: the general assembly shall enact no special legislation relative to the powers, organization, terms of elective offices or form of government of any single town, city or borough

claim: Any municipality may adopt and amend its own charter
quote: adopt and amend a charter which shall be its organic law

claim: A charter must give the municipality a legislative body: town meeting, representative town meeting, board of selectmen, council, board of directors, aldermen or burgesses
quote: (A) A town meeting; (B) a representative town meeting; (C) a board of selectmen, council, board of directors, board of aldermen or board of burgesses

claim: Petition candidates sign on forms warning that only electors may sign
quote: YOU MAY NOT SIGN THIS PETITION

claim: The warning says a signer must be an elector
quote: IF YOU ARE NOT AN ELECTOR

claim: Towns of 10,000 or more may have up to six other selectmen
quote: in the case of any town having a population of ten thousand or more, not more than six other selectmen

claim: The constitution's home rule article covers towns, cities and boroughs
quote: relative to the powers, organization, and form of government of such political subdivisions
